app_note: Calcium appears in fortified foods as several salts.
risk_note: Absorption and health claims vary by form and context.

app_note: Iron is often added to enriched grains and cereals.
risk_note: Too much iron can be harmful for some people; claims need care.

app_note: Potassium chloride can replace some sodium chloride in lower-sodium foods.
risk_note: Kidney-related cautions need precise wording.

app_note: Magnesium appears in fortified foods and mineral blends.
risk_note: Supplement claims and laxative effects vary by form.

app_note: Zinc salts are common in fortified foods and supplements.
risk_note: Excess zinc can affect copper balance; cite carefully.

app_note: Iodized salt is a major public-health fortification example.
risk_note: Thyroid-related claims need careful sourcing.

app_note: Selenium is needed only in trace amounts.
risk_note: Excess intake risk means claims require source review.

app_note: Copper can appear as a trace mineral fortifier.
risk_note: High intake can be harmful; source review required.

app_note: Manganese appears in trace mineral blends.
risk_note: Avoid neurological claims without source review.

app_note: Chromium is sometimes added to diet and sports products.
risk_note: Blood-sugar claims require strong evidence review.

app_note: Molybdenum is a trace mineral found in some fortification formulas.
risk_note: Usually not common on ordinary labels.

app_note: Sodium is essential but also heavily tracked on nutrition labels.
risk_note: High sodium intake is a common dietary concern.

app_note: Chloride usually appears paired with sodium or potassium.
risk_note: Rarely listed separately except in formulas.

app_note: Phosphorus appears both naturally and as phosphate additives.
risk_note: Kidney-related context requires careful wording.

app_note: Fluoride is more often a water or salt fortification topic than a normal ingredient-list item.
risk_note: Regulatory context varies strongly.

app_note: Silicon dioxide is often used to keep powders flowing.
risk_note: As a nutrient topic it needs separate evidence review.

app_note: Boron appears mostly in supplements rather than ordinary food ingredient lists.
risk_note: Avoid health claims without review.

app_note: Nickel is more relevant as a trace exposure than an intentional food ingredient.
risk_note: Sensitivity and contaminant context need review.

app_note: Cobalt is part of vitamin B12 chemistry.
risk_note: Usually tracked through B12 rather than as cobalt itself.

functional_purpose: component of amino acids and additives
app_note: Sulfur occurs naturally in foods and in some additives.
risk_note: Sulfites are a separate sensitivity category.
